answer: A cipher ledger can anchor a tri-role rotation: every newcomer cycles through proposer, checker, and arbiter across three seasons, each role graded blind by strangers from other roles. Standing grows only when all three pass, like shale layers pressing into solid rock — one thin sheet proves nothing, but the stack holds weight. A ferrous bond, posted at entry and slashed on any failed grade, makes each role costly to fake. One operator cannot staff dozens of identities through three demanding roles at once, because each role needs different skills and fresh evidence.
